newsitem.title: UK: Czarnikow sees India 96/97 sugar output 13 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Czarnikow sees India 96/97 sugar output 13 mln t.

text.p: India's sugar output from its 1996/97 cane harvest could slump to as little as 13.0 million tonnes white value after the record 16.45 million tonnes in 1995/96, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.

Noting that its previous Indian estimate was based on a crop of 13.8 million tonnes, Czarnikow said even though production to mid-February was only 827,000 tonnes behind last year's corresponding level, the gap would widen.

"Even though the crop last year went on to finish at a record 16.45 million tonnes, the gap this year is expected to widen after May when milling is expected to wind down prematurely for lack of cane," it said.
"Our last estimate was based on a crop of 13.8 million tonnes but latest reports suggest that even 13.0 million tonnes may be difficult to achieve."

Czarnikow said while India's potential exports were previously thought to be little higher than one million tonnes, this estimate was being reduced as any surpluses would certainly be needed by the 1997/98 season.

"Most expect that there will be yet a further declien in production before the trend can be turned round while at the same time consumption continues to rise at some five percent a year or more," the report said.

Another factor was that mills had not been encouraged to export at levels which they saw as a loss, after comparing sales at world and domestic market prices. Czarnikow noted that the government had not yet placed any restraints on sugar exports.
